title: Mohd Arshad v. Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
disposition: Pending clause 6.5 representation directed to be decided within four weeks.
headnote: Writ seeking bill rectification disposed of without any opinion on merits. Respondent no. 2 directed to decide the pending representation dated 01.03.2023 under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, in accordance with law, within four weeks of production of a certified copy and the representation, after a reasonable opportunity of hearing.
facts: Mohd Arshad, a consumer of Purvanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., sought rectification of his electricity bill. He submitted a representation dated 1 March 2023 before respondent no. 2, which was still pending when he approached the High Court in Writ-C No. 12555 of 2023. On instructions, counsel for the licensees told the Court that respondent no. 2 would decide that representation under clause 6.5 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 within four weeks, after giving the consumer a reasonable opportunity of hearing.

holding_units.holding: Where the consumer's representation dated 01.03.2023 seeking bill rectification and invoking clause 6.5 is already pending, the writ is disposed of without any opinion on merits, and respondent no. 2 is directed to decide that representation in accordance with law within four weeks of production of a certified copy of the order and a copy of the representation, after affording a reasonable opportunity of hearing.

principle_tags.application: The representation dated 01.03.2023 invoking clause 6.5 was pending; the licensee was directed to decide it on a hearing, in accordance with law, within four weeks.
Because the clause 6.5 representation was already pending, the writ was disposed of without a counter-affidavit and without any opinion on the bill.

not_decided.point: Correctness of the electricity bill and the merits of the representation dated 01.03.2023
not_decided.note: The Court disposed of the writ without expressing any opinion on merits, leaving the representation to be decided under clause 6.5.
